The fixtures `test/fixtures/Toast*.vue` hold the components of the tests.

`Toast.test.ts` tests the action: its `<button type="button">`, `as`, the content of `actionProps.children` over the slot, the attributes and listeners of `actionProps`, and no render with no content. The part reads its element, so it has no `nativeButton`.
`Toast.test.ts` tests the arrow: `aria-hidden` and the side of its positioner, and the error outside a positioner.
`Toast.test.ts` tests the close button: its `<button type="button">`, the close at a press, and `aria-hidden` and no tab stop while the stack is collapsed (VUE-232).
`Toast.test.ts` tests the content: `data-behind`, `data-expanded` and a new measure of the root when the content changes.

`provider.test.ts` and `Toast.test.ts` test the manager: `add`, `update`, `close` and `promise` in each provider from the mount to the unmount, the timers of an update, and the promise of each provider (VUE-90). The list has the open toasts only, and `<TransitionGroup>` around the roots animates their enter and leave, so the parts have no transition status and no `data-starting-style` or `data-ending-style`.

`Toast.test.ts` tests the description: its `

`, its id in `aria-describedby`, and the name of a toast with no title (VUE-99).
`Toast.test.ts` tests the title: its `<h2>`, its id in `aria-labelledby`, and an empty `id` (VUE-93).
`Toast.test.ts` tests the portal: the viewport in `<body>`, and in place with no portal. The portal renders no element of its own.

`Toast.test.ts` tests the positioner: the place at the anchor of `positionerProps`, a prop of the part over `positionerProps`, the defaults with no anchor, `--toast-index`, and a positioner in `<TransitionGroup>` with `duration`. A positioner in its leave keeps its last index, because Vue does not patch an element that leaves.

`provider.test.ts` tests the provider: a change of `timeout` and `limit` that a part below reads in the same update, and the timers. Vue has no `Activity`, and a part keeps no state about `KeepAlive`, so the provider has no pause for a held branch.

`Toast.test.ts` tests the root: the role, the variables, the ids, Escape (VUE-127), the priority `high`, the `inert` of a limited toast and the leave in `<TransitionGroup>`. `Toast.swipe.test.ts` tests the swipe with a real pointer. A list with an index key gives a root another toast, so a list of toasts needs `:key="toast.id"`, as the Vue guide asks. The attribute that stops a swipe has one name, `data-vase-ui-swipe-ignore`, and no second name `data-swipe-ignore`. The list has the open toasts only, and `<TransitionGroup>` around the roots animates their enter and leave, so the parts have no transition status and no `data-starting-style` or `data-ending-style`.

`provider.test.ts` and `Toast.test.ts` test the list and the timers: the time that is left at a stop, a full time for a timer with no time left, and each state that stops the timers. The list has the open toasts only, and `<TransitionGroup>` around the roots animates their enter and leave, so the parts have no transition status and no `data-starting-style` or `data-ending-style`.

`Toast.test.ts` tests the composable: `add`, `update`, `close`, `promise`, `limit`, `timeout`, the ids and the list with the parts. The list has the open toasts only, and `<TransitionGroup>` around the roots animates their enter and leave, so the parts have no transition status and no `data-starting-style` or `data-ending-style`.
`Toast.test.ts` tests the content rule of the label parts: `0` is content, and an empty text, `null` and a Boolean are none. A part cannot read the children of a vnode.
`Toast.test.ts` tests the label parts: the render only with content, a label that is a function, the last title and description (VUE-56), and the `element` slot.

`Toast.test.ts` tests the viewport: the region, F6, Tab and Shift+Tab with the sentinels, the tab stop of the viewport while a toast of high priority has none (VUE-232), Escape (VUE-130), the focus at a close, the hover, the window and the page (BUG-6174, VUE-76), and the alerts. The developer gives the viewport an `aria-label` in the language of the page, so the viewport has no default name.

With a Vue default, the part cannot find out that a prop is absent. The props of the placement thus have no Vue default. A prop that is absent takes the same key of `positionerProps` of the toast, else the default of Base UI: `'top'` for `side`, `'center'` for `align`, 0 for `sideOffset` and `alignOffset`, 5 for `arrowPadding` and `collisionPadding`, `'clipping-ancestors'` for `collisionBoundary`, `'absolute'` for `positionMethod`, and `false` for `sticky` and `disableAnchorTracking`.

returnTypeDifferences.reason: The source of Base UI returns the same type, `ToastManager<Data>`. Its `types.md` prints the type argument as `{}`.

`setup` runs one time, so a plain array does not follow a change of the toasts. `toasts` of the result is thus a `ComputedRef` of the array. The source of Base UI returns `UseToastManagerReturnValue<Data>`, and its `types.md` prints the type argument as `{}`.
